title: A point of a limit is the limit of its images
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ and projections $f_i:S\to S_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $s\in S$ and $s_i=f_i(s)$. Then the field maps $\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(s_{i'})$ ($i'\ge i$) and $\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(s)$ induced by $f_{i'i}$ and $f_i$ [def-weil-residue-field] make $\kappa(s)$ the directed colimit $\varinjlim_i\kappa(s_i)$; equivalently $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, with the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$, is the limit of the inverse system $(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i))_i$ (whose transition morphisms are affine) in the category of schemes, compatibly with the canonical morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)\to S_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$.

source.place: Limits, Lemma Tag 0CUG (lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles, line 332), part (1), and its proof (reduction to S_i affine, then A/p = colim A_i/p_i)
